format: 每张2列3行：前五格为五个独立关卡，右下格为已展示关卡的另一个观察面。
scope: 每一关只展示食光兽局部，不展示全兽或完整头部。镜头构图与光鳞位置概念图，未做几何光路或可玩性验证。

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a storyboard sheet of rough 2D side-scrolling game BACKGROUND SCREENS, not a site map or an isometric illustration.
Primary intent: illustrate actual player-camera framing for a poetic puzzle game where a thumb-sized protagonist redirects light toward a SMALL EXPOSED PART of ONE enormous immobile light-eating beast embedded in an abandoned botanical garden. Every screen must be a CLOSE LOCAL VIEW. The creature is far larger than the camera: only a small surface patch or partial body contour can fit in any panel.
FORMAT: a large square sheet, preferably 3072x3072, with exactly SIX equal wide 16:9 landscape panels in a TWO-COLUMN by THREE-ROW grid, clear white gutters. Five numbered level background sketches in reading order (upper left, upper right, middle left, middle right, lower left); lower right is an explicitly labelled alternative camera view of one of those five SAME locations. No extra panels. One small Chinese sheet title at top. Each panel has a concise Chinese caption OUTSIDE and above its picture. Keep text minimal, legible, exactly as provided. This is an annotated storyboard sheet rather than final production art.
CAMERA: nearly orthographic SIDE ELEVATION, eye-level, fixed platform-game camera. Predominantly horizontal walkable baseline, with occasional step, thin rope, vine or ladder linking heights. Use foreground silhouettes, a clear playable midground and softer background to suggest depth in a flat image. Architecture can be cut away to reveal room interiors. Walls show real windows, cracks and apertures. Limited perspective depth is allowed only for visible sidewalls or alternative observation faces. NO top-down view. NO axonometric/isometric view. NO floating diorama or entire world on a plinth. NO wide overview, NO entire beast, NO complete head, NO complete paw or isolated complete limb.
STYLE: restrained rough graphite/charcoal linework with a few muted moss-green, misty blue-gray and warm cream washes; quiet poetic atmosphere, soft daylight, simple large forms, unfinished thumbnail background design. Low detail, strong silhouettes and clear spatial relationships. Foreground darkest, background lightest. Warm amber is reserved for the actual sunlight and local feeding scale. Not a polished watercolor landscape, not a black horror scene.
SCALE AND BEAST: include one consistent tiny black protagonist silhouette in EVERY main panel, about 1/15 to 1/20 of panel height, walking on the visible baseline. Scale objects accordingly: terracotta pot or shelf as room-scale, dew as head-size, a leaf as a canopy. The beast's cropped living surface is pale warm gray, subtle irregular soft scales, sparse moss and fibrous texture, visibly organic rather than a separate rock or a second small animal. Its surface naturally extends out of frame. Indicate just ONE small translucent almond/petal-shaped feeding scale on the exposed skin, with gentle amber glow; it is living tissue, not a lamp or golden machine. No wounds, blood or interior organs. The rest of the creature remains offscreen behind earth/building/foliage. Never put a miniature complete animal in the scene.
GAME CONTENT: show a few major interactive props clearly: pivoting mirror shards, rotating leaf supports with dew, metal reflectors, prism, shutter. Include a simple plausible sunlight path entering from a real opening and reflecting toward the feeding scale; no beam passing through solid walls. This is a compositional light-path sketch, not a complex solved wiring diagram. A small exit opening, walkway or vine at screen edge links to the next level. Do not add UI, inventory, health bars, world map, compass, level-flow arrows or diagram boxes inside the scenes.
CRITICAL PRIORITY: all panels read as distinct playable 2D side-view local backgrounds. Only the specified small body portion is visible; even later levels must NEVER reveal the whole beast.
SHEET TITLE exactly: '食光兽｜01—05 局部场景背景草图'.
PANEL 1, TOP LEFT. Caption '01 门槛苔地｜尾尖表皮'. Outdoor ground-level side view. A huge iron gate bar and mossy stone threshold on left; tiny protagonist enters left and can walk right. Only a small rounded pale-gray tail surface protrudes beneath the stone ledge at right and continues completely OFF the right edge. It is not a whole tail. One little pivoting shard mirror planted in a twig support near center sends a sliver of sunlight through the gate bars to a feeding scale under the ledge. Show the dark rim of a distant pot at far right as exit continuity. No complete beast silhouette in sky.
PANEL 2, TOP RIGHT. Caption '02 倒扣陶盆｜尾部光鳞'. Inside an enormous overturned cracked terracotta pot, shown as a SIDE CUTAWAY arch. The ceiling's drain hole admits a shaft of sunlight. Roots hang like curtains; a leaf on a pivoting stem supports one large dew drop that focuses light. A small exposed section of the SAME tail surface is trapped behind the inner right clay edge and extends out of frame under soil. Tail scale visible there. Tiny protagonist on pot-bottom soil; left entry crack; low right outlet leads to drain. Never a small beast sitting inside pot.
PANEL 3, MIDDLE LEFT. Caption '03 排水暗渠｜尾根表皮'. Side section of a low horizontal underground masonry drain. Solid ceiling with TWO actual grating openings admitting daylight from above. Narrow dry maintenance ledge beside shallow water for tiny character. A substantially wider but still incomplete pale-gray tail-root surface presses through a broken right wall, extending beyond frame. Two small silver metal fragments on swivel pins turn a thin light beam from ceiling to target. Right lower opening leads onward to pond. All light travels within open culvert, not through bricks.
PANEL 4, MIDDLE RIGHT. Caption '04 蓄水浅池｜下腹局部'. Outdoor side-on view at water level; broad still pond surface runs horizontally across image, thick reed stems and stepping leaves create clear foreground traversable silhouettes. At far bank on right, only a low cropped curve of the beast's lower belly presses against embankment, pale-gray skin emerging beneath roots, rest OFFSCREEN. One leaf-mounted mirror redirects sunlight toward water and up to a small skin scale. Tiny character stands on reed bridge. Small pipe opening/pump-house wall at far right links next stage. Do not show complete animal torso, neck, limbs, face or legs.
PANEL 5, BOTTOM LEFT. Caption '05 废弃泵房｜侧腹局部'. INSIDE a tall abandoned pump room shown side-on with the front wall cut away. A distinct HIGH RECTANGULAR WINDOW at upper LEFT with one broken lower-right pane and a diagonal copper pipe is the recognition anchor. Sunlight comes through that real window, hits a small copper mirror wheel operated by a fine cord near floor-center, then lands on a narrow organic flank patch visible through a crack in the lower RIGHT wall. Thick pipes and one old wheel as background shapes, no machinery clutter. Tiny protagonist near wheel. Low right inspection hole is exit to greenhouse.
PANEL 6, BOTTOM RIGHT. Caption '05 另一观察面｜泵房室外'. This is the EXACT SAME pump room as panel 5, seen from its OUTSIDE left wall in a flat side elevation, not a new level. Show the SAME high rectangular window with broken lower-right pane and the SAME diagonal copper pipe clearly. A small exterior hinged mirror on the window ledge can aim sunlight through the opening. Include tiny protagonist on outside maintenance ledge. A subtle sightline through the window reveals the interior copper reflector, and a cut-away edge hints at the same tiny flank patch. Keep the building local and heavily cropped, no whole structure overview. This paired image demonstrates a viewpoint change while keeping physical window and optics in the same location.

SHEET TITLE exactly: '食光兽｜06—10 局部场景背景草图'.
CONTINUITY IN THIS SHEET: panels 06,07,08 belong to the SAME tall greenhouse at successive heights. Repeat a distinctive blue-gray vertical iron column with a small X brace and a twisting ivy stem at the RIGHT edge across all three. Never depict three separate greenhouse buildings.
PANEL 1, TOP LEFT. Caption '06 温室苗床｜肋侧局部'. Inside greenhouse at floor/seed-bed level, strictly 2D side elevation. Ferns make large overhead canopies; planting troughs form waist-high ledges for the tiny protagonist. A small pale-gray organic flank/rib patch protrudes through the broken base of the rear wall at RIGHT, with only one broad curved surface and feeding scale visible, no entire belly or ribs. Ceiling glass admits daylight; a hinged leaf shutter and twig-mounted mirror guide the beam down into the shaded trough toward the skin. The blue-gray X-braced column and winding ivy form rightward climb to next stage.
PANEL 2, TOP RIGHT. Caption '07 叶幕走廊｜背侧局部'. The SAME greenhouse upper horizontal catwalk, seen side-on at leaf height. Broad leaves form staggered light-blocking planes above and behind the path; root/cable suspended mirror rotates. Show only an angled strip of the same beast's upper flank/back skin through a broken rear window at right, extending off right and bottom edges. A bright gap through overlapping leaves permits the beam to reach a feeding scale; leaf hinges make operations readable. Tiny protagonist on iron catwalk. Recognizable X-braced right column/ivy; broken upper-right glass exit leads to roof.
PANEL 3, MIDDLE LEFT. Caption '08 雨槽屋脊｜背脊表皮'. Outside on greenhouse roof at close scale, side elevation. A deep U-shaped gutter is the protagonist's walkable trough, glass roof slopes recede only slightly behind it. Cropped pale-gray dorsal ridge fills the shaded background at right like an organic wall and extends beyond both right and upper frame; NO entire back or animal silhouette. A sliding mirror foot on the gutter and a small tilted metal flashing redirect sunlight into one shaded feeding scale at the gutter/skin interface. The same X-braced column is glimpsed below roof glass. Gutter visibly extends horizontally to an attic window frame at far right.
PANEL 4, MIDDLE RIGHT. Caption '09 园丁阁楼｜肩部局部'. Side-on attic interior, low slanted roof at top, giant seed envelopes and a folded old glove on a shelf indicate thumb scale. Entry gutter ends at left window. A skylight and small old hand mirror plus magnifying lens create a short light path through a low real wall crack on right to an exposed SHOULDER PATCH outside. Only the patch is seen, not an arm or complete shoulder anatomy; surface extends offscreen. Tiny protagonist on wooden floor. Recognizable right wall vent has ivy entering and leads onward.
PANEL 5, BOTTOM LEFT. Caption '10 常春藤坡｜肩颈局部'. Exterior close side view of a gently ascending ivy/root path. One enormous organic shoulder-to-neck surface forms the entire right/back wall, heavily cropped so anatomy remains partial. Thumb-sized hero climbs from lower left to upper right on roots. A leaf support with a dew drop and a reflective shard lodged in a vine knot guide sunlight onto the neck-side scale. Tower masonry and a broken low window enter only the far-right edge, providing the next entrance. No head, eye, antlers or full animal.
PANEL 6, BOTTOM RIGHT. Caption '07 另一观察面｜叶幕下方'. Alternative side-on camera position beneath the SAME 07 greenhouse catwalk, not another level. Repeat the X-braced blue-gray iron column, ivy, three distinctive overlapping leaves, suspended mirror and same light scale behind rear window. From below, reveal the previously hidden small gap BETWEEN leaves that light can pass through, plus the underside of the catwalk; show a tiny protagonist as scale. Keep this a usable layered 2D screen, no isometric cutaway building.

ABSOLUTE FRAMING RULE: the late game does NOT reveal the whole beast in these backgrounds. In panel 12 only a cropped horn ROOT and adjacent neck skin are allowed. In panel 13 only a FRAGMENT of one enormous eyelid/eye surface fits, with no complete eye outline or face. Panel 15 only a small chest surface and feeding tissue, not the complete chest or embracing arms. Do not add a giant animal in distant scenery.
PANEL 1, TOP LEFT. Caption '11 观测暗室｜颈侧局部'. Flat side-on observatory room with thick masonry, a tall narrow slit window on LEFT, and a vertical dividing wall with one OFFSET ventilation opening. Inside sit one simple prism and two small hinged mirrors, with a visible beam entering the window, bending at mirrors and passing through the actual divider opening. At right, a damaged wall exposes a narrow strip of neck skin and feeding scale, rest outside frame. Tiny hero on floor, spiral stair starts at far right and exits upward. Show open space between optics and target, not light penetrating wall.
PANEL 2, TOP RIGHT. Caption '12 露天观星台｜角根局部'. Close SIDE VIEW of rooftop deck, NOT an establishing shot. Tiny hero at lower left beside an observation mirror lever and hanging counterweight. A huge pale fibrous HORN ROOT enters from bottom-right and exits through top-right of frame; horn TIP is out of frame. Adjacent neck skin shows one small light scale at deck level, no head or entire antler. Only local deck rail, floor and misty sky behind. Sun strikes observation mirror and is redirected onto that skin scale. Exterior maintenance ladder descends beyond left edge toward next gallery.
PANEL 3, MIDDLE LEFT. Caption '13 面颊花廊｜眼睑旁局部'. Intimate 2D side-elevation flower gallery, a narrow horizontal rail/path across lower quarter of image, tiny hero standing on it at left, petal shutter and little mirror nearby. Behind the path the beast's eye region is so enormous that ONLY a cropped segment of the curved eyelid and a small portion of eye surface fit in the upper-right background, extending outside top and right edges. Do NOT draw complete eye, snout, head or face. A small feeding scale beside the eyelid is the amber light target, NOT the eyeball. Soft floral foreground, delicate sense of a quiet living presence. Gallery/irrigation channel exits down/right.
PANEL 4, MIDDLE RIGHT. Caption '14 暖房根室｜胸侧局部'. Side section of half-buried ruined conservatory root cellar. Roots hang from ceiling, a real lightwell opens at upper-left, a small suspended mirror and a second ground mirror turn incoming sunlight through gaps between roots. Right rear wall is partly broken and exposes a broad but incomplete chest-side skin surface with faint light veins leading right, no organs. Tiny hero on low brick ledge. A broken right wall opening at same floor level is the exit to central garden. The main architecture is clearly enclosed despite the illustration's cutaway front.
PANEL 5, BOTTOM LEFT. Caption '15 中央心庭｜胸前光鳞'. Close 2D side view of sunken outdoor seed garden, NOT a courtyard overview. A narrow soil path and germinating plants at lower foreground, tiny hero beside small old ring-mirror assembly operated by light cord. The background/right is one huge cropped warm-gray chest surface continuing beyond top/right borders. A translucent living petal-shaped feeding scale glows gently within the skin; a few converging light veins identify chest location. A genuine sky opening above lets sun reach the mirror and scale. No complete arms, body, animal head, full beast silhouette or entire garden. A few tiny shoots and calm warm light suggest new life.
PANEL 6, BOTTOM RIGHT. Caption '11 另一观察面｜错位通光孔'. The SAME observatory dark room from a second fixed SIDE observation face around its corner; retain narrow left slit window, dividing wall, offset ventilation aperture, prism, mirrors and neck-skin target. This view makes it clear that the wall aperture is offset in depth, and reveals a second reflector hidden behind its edge. Include a tiny protagonist on the same baseline. Real beam passes through the open vent and reaches the same local neck scale. Do not convert to an isometric room map. Use modest 2D layered depth and cropped wall edge to explain the changed viewpoint.
